subject: Order form — staggered invoicing, usage netting & tax alignment
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>
To: Orchid AP <ap@orchidai.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jul 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Order form — staggered invoicing, usage netting & tax alignment

Hi Maya / AP team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to propose an invoicing cadence and a simple netting approach for the Order Form so your procurement and finance teams can forecast. High level proposal: 

- Pricing schedule: monthly invoices that reflect actual usage with an agreed minimum commit per quarter (example Q3 min commit = $60,000).
- Staggered ramp: Q3 has a 3-month ramp (40% / 30% / 30% allocation of the quarter minimum), thereafter standard monthly billing against the monthly target.
- Netting / credits: underutilization in a month will be credited against future invoices within the same quarter; overage billed in the next invoice. No cash refunds — credits only.
- Activation fee: one-time activation fee invoiced on the first invoice.
- Net terms: prefer Net60 but open to discussion if your AP team needs Net45/Net30.
- Taxes: customer to remit VAT/GST where applicable; Redwood will issue VAT-compliant invoices and can provide supporting evidence. If reverse-charge applies, we'll reflect that on the invoice but need confirmation from you.

Can you confirm whether a monthly split + quarterly minimum commit with netting credits is acceptable? Also: do you require a PO before the first invoice, and what net terms does Orchid prefer?

If helpful I can attach a redlined Order Form that shows line-item invoicing.

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form — staggered invoicing, usage netting & tax alignment

Rafael,

Thanks — this looks sensible. A few notes from AP/procurement: 

- Net terms: Orchid standard is Net45; smaller vendors are sometimes Net30, but we can accept Net45 for this pilot.
- PO: procurement prefers to issue a PO before the first invoice. Can Redwood accept a PO issuance window of 5 business days prior to first invoice?
- Activation fee: we prefer the activation fee shown as a separate line item on invoice #1.
- VAT/GST: Orchid is EU-registered in several countries; we will share VAT registration info if you confirm Redwood will keep VAT on invoices when applicable. If reverse-charge is appropriate for some countries, we'll confirm per-entity.

I can loop in our AP manager if needed. Attaching my quick notes below.

Best,

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form — staggered invoicing, usage netting & tax alignment

Maya — thanks for the quick reply. Looping in Kim (legal) and Ben (finance) to confirm a workable commercial path. Below are the adjusted asks from Redwood and a suggested redline approach: 

1) Invoicing cadence
- Redwood will issue monthly invoices (by the 5th business day of the following month) showing: activation fee (if applicable), monthly usage, and invoice-level credits/debits (netting for prior under/over usage).

2) Minimum commit + ramp
- Quarter minimum agreed per Order Form; for Q3 we propose $60k with a 3-month ramp (40%/30%/30%). Credits for underuse accrue and are applied to subsequent invoices within the same quarter; any residual shortfall at quarter close is invoiced as a true-up.

3) Net terms and PO
- Redwood standard Net60. Given Orchid's preference, we can accept Net45 for the pilot. We can also accept a PO issued up to 5 business days prior to first invoice, but we need the PO number before sending invoice #1.

4) Taxes
- Redwood will charge VAT where required and provide VAT invoices. If reverse-charge applies for Orchid entities, we will not charge VAT but will include the appropriate note; we need the VAT registration numbers per entity.

5) Currency and gross-up
- Invoices will be issued in USD unless otherwise specified on the Order Form. If Orchid requires local-currency billing for any entity, we should include gross-up language for tax withholding.

I have attached a redline that implements the monthly line-item split and the netting mechanism. Can Kim and Ben confirm the PO/Net-term language and any finance/legal constraints? Maya — can you confirm the PO timing and send VAT registration details for the entities we should treat as reverse-charge?

Attachments: Orchid_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Rafael

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@orchidai.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form — staggered invoicing, usage netting & tax alignment

Rafael / Ben / Maya — I reviewed the redline. A few legal / procurement items to lock down before we finalize: 

- PO requirement: acceptable to require a PO prior to the first invoice but we should add a fallback that allows invoicing to proceed if PO is delayed provided Orchid signs the Order Form; Redwood's standard is PO before invoice but we can be flexible for pilot customers.
- Net terms: Net45 is fine for the pilot. We will update the Order Form language to show Net45 as a mutually agreed deviation and keep Net60 as our default in master terms.
- Minimum commit true-up: clarify timing — crediting during the quarter is fine, but any residual shortfall will be invoiced within 10 business days after quarter close. Add explicit language to prevent double-crediting and to cap credits to the quarter minimum.
- Tax language: Redwood will charge VAT where legally required. If reverse-charge applies, Orchid must provide VAT numbers and a statement per-entity. Also include a gross-up clause for withholding taxes if any jurisdiction requires it.
- Currency: add an exhibit showing currency per-bill-to entity.

I'll attach the Redwood VAT playbook for Orchid's AP team and a short redline summary. Once we have the PO timing confirmed and VAT numbers, legal can prepare the final doc for signature.

Attachments: Redwood_VAT_Playbook.pdf

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com

Rafael / Kim / Ben — thanks, all. Procurement confirms they can issue PO #7845 three business days before go-live (slightly tighter than the 5-day window but acceptable). VAT numbers attached separately via secure portal; we'll share entity-level numbers by EOD Monday.

Orchid accepts Net45 for the pilot and the crediting/netting approach. One minor ask: can Redwood delay any true-up invoicing until we confirm final country residency of some of our entities (we expect to provide that within the quarter)? If not, we accept the 10-business-day true-up window.

Please send the final Order Form for signature and DocuSign link; we'll sign and route PO at our end immediately after. I've attached our PO stub for your reference.
